items.s: A good torch is ___ on a camping trip.
items.tip: in- + dispense + -able (drop the e): indispensable = absolutely necessary.
items.say: A good torch is indispensable on a camping trip.
items.ask: A good torch is blank on a camping trip.

items.s: Our school team had an ___ run of twenty wins in a row.
items.tip: un- + precedent + -ed: unprecedented = never happened before.
items.say: Our school team had an unprecedented run of twenty wins in a row.
items.ask: Our school team had an blank run of twenty wins in a row.

items.s: Grandma's old teddy bear is ___ to me.
items.tip: ir- + replace + -able. Keep the e after c so it still sounds like s: irreplaceable.
items.say: Grandma's old teddy bear is irreplaceable to me.
items.ask: Grandma's old teddy bear is blank to me.

items.s: It's ___ that anyone could eat fifty pancakes in one go!
items.tip: in- + conceive + -able (drop the e): impossible to imagine.
items.say: It's inconceivable that anyone could eat fifty pancakes in one go!
items.ask: It's blank that anyone could eat fifty pancakes in one go!

items.s: Shouting at a scared puppy is ___. It only makes things worse.
items.tip: counter- (against) + productive: it works against what you want.
items.say: Shouting at a scared puppy is counterproductive. It only makes things worse.
items.ask: Shouting at a scared puppy is blank. It only makes things worse.

items.s: The instructions were ___, so we didn't need any help.
items.tip: self- + explanatory (explain loses its i): it explains itself.
items.say: The instructions were self-explanatory, so we didn't need any help.
items.ask: The instructions were blank, so we didn't need any help.

items.s: The class voted ___ for a longer lunch break.
items.tip: over- + whelm + -ing + -ly: four parts make one adverb meaning 'by a huge number'.
items.say: The class voted overwhelmingly for a longer lunch break.
items.ask: The class voted blank for a longer lunch break.

items.s: Our cat ___ wakes me up at six, even at weekends.
items.tip: in- + vary (y → i) + -able + -ly: invariably = always, without change.
items.say: Our cat invariably wakes me up at six, even at weekends.
items.ask: Our cat blank wakes me up at six, even at weekends.

items.s: The firefighters acted ___ to save the kittens.
items.tip: hero → heroic → heroically: -ic adjectives make adverbs with -ally.
items.say: The firefighters acted heroically to save the kittens.
items.ask: The firefighters acted blank to save the kittens.

items.s: Laughing at someone's mistake is ___.
items.tip: sense → sensitive (drop the e, add -itive) → in- for 'not': insensitive.
items.say: Laughing at someone's mistake is insensitive.
items.ask: Laughing at someone's mistake is blank.

items.s: The top shelf is ___ to little children.
items.tip: in- + access + -ible (not -able): inaccessible = can't be reached.
items.say: The top shelf is inaccessible to little children.
items.ask: The top shelf is blank to little children.

items.s: The twin puppies were almost ___. We couldn't tell them apart!
items.tip: in- + distinguish + -able: impossible to tell apart.
items.say: The twin puppies were almost indistinguishable. We couldn't tell them apart!
items.ask: The twin puppies were almost blank. We couldn't tell them apart!

items.s: The judges loved the ___ of Mia's drawings.
items.tip: original + -ity = originality (the quality of being new and different).
items.say: The judges loved the originality of Mia's drawings.
items.ask: The judges loved the blank of Mia's drawings.

items.s: The team's ___ to give up helped them win the final.
items.tip: refuse → refusal (drop the e, add -al): the noun after The team's.
items.say: The team's refusal to give up helped them win the final.
items.ask: The team's blank to give up helped them win the final.

items.s: The ___ of the giant redwood trees amazed us.
items.tip: -ent adjectives make -ence nouns: magnificent → magnificence.
items.say: The magnificence of the giant redwood trees amazed us.
items.ask: The blank of the giant redwood trees amazed us.

items.s: The cat stared ___ at the fish tank.
items.tip: long (to want) → longing → longingly: an adverb describing how it stared.
items.say: The cat stared longingly at the fish tank.
items.ask: The cat stared blank at the fish tank.

items.s: The class cheered ___ when the winner was announced.
items.tip: enthusiasm → enthusiastic → enthusiastically (-ic + -ally).
items.say: The class cheered enthusiastically when the winner was announced.
items.ask: The class cheered blank when the winner was announced.

items.s: The goalkeeper gets a ___ amount of blame when the team loses.
items.tip: dis- + proportion + -ate: disproportionate = too big compared with the rest.
items.say: The goalkeeper gets a disproportionate amount of blame when the team loses.
items.ask: The goalkeeper gets a blank amount of blame when the team loses.

items.s: The dinosaur fossil was ___ well preserved.
items.tip: remark → remarkable → remarkably (-le → -ly): an adverb before well.
items.say: The dinosaur fossil was remarkably well preserved.
items.ask: The dinosaur fossil was blank well preserved.

items.s: Ollie's handwriting was so messy that it was ___.
items.tip: legible starts with l, so its opposite takes il-: illegible = impossible to read.
items.say: Ollie's handwriting was so messy that it was illegible.
items.ask: Ollie's handwriting was so messy that it was blank.

items.s: The cat looked at the new vacuum cleaner with great ___.
items.tip: suspect → suspicion: the noun after with great; the t changes to c and we add -ion.
items.say: The cat looked at the new vacuum cleaner with great suspicion.
items.ask: The cat looked at the new vacuum cleaner with great blank.

items.s: The old map was written in a code that was ___ to us.
items.tip: in- + comprehend (d → s) + -ible: impossible to understand.
items.say: The old map was written in a code that was incomprehensible to us.
items.ask: The old map was written in a code that was blank to us.

items.s: Ava's poster was ___ the best in the competition.
items.tip: un- + question + -able + -ly: unquestionably = without any doubt.
items.say: Ava's poster was unquestionably the best in the competition.
items.ask: Ava's poster was blank the best in the competition.

items.s: We tested the robot many times to check its ___.
items.tip: rely → reliable (y → i) → reliability (-able → -ability).
items.say: We tested the robot many times to check its reliability.
items.ask: We tested the robot many times to check its blank.
